proofUses.reason: The corrected bound uses absolute values of the three reciprocal factors. A finite-support counterexample diagnoses the missing positivity qualification; the entry remains provisional.
Positive denominators allow the original difference bound. The comparison keeps its factor two and the full majorant has no zero except the omitted k=0 frequency.
A first-exit convolution has finite support and mass less than one. Its geometric expansion gives weighted moments; the uniform coupling and domination then give weighted-norm continuity.
The k=0 quotient is omitted explicitly. A uniform weighted-norm bound handles k approaching zero before taking suprema. The improvement implication remains a hypothesis.
